ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A certain diploid plant’s P1 and P2 plants are crossed to obtain F1, and F1 is selfed to obtain F2. PCR detection is performed on the DNA of individuals, and the electrophoresis results of the products are shown in the figure, among which ①～⑧ are some F2 individuals. The upper 2 bands are amplification products of a pair of allelic genes, and the lower 2 bands are amplification products of another pair of allelic genes. These 2 pairs of allelic genes are located on non-homologous chromosomes. Answer the question: What is the proportion of the selfed progeny of ① whose PCR product electrophoresis result is the same as the electrophoresis result of ④?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A certain diploid plant’s P1 and P2 plants are crossed to obtain F1, and F1 is selfed to obtain F2. PCR detection is performed on the DNA of individuals, and the electrophoresis results of the products are shown in the figure, among which ①～⑧ are some F2 individuals. The upper 2 bands are amplification products of a pair of allelic genes, and the lower 2 bands are amplification products of another pair of allelic genes. These 2 pairs of allelic genes are located on non-homologous chromosomes. Answer the question: What is the proportion of the selfed progeny of ① whose PCR product electrophoresis result is the same as the electrophoresis result of ④?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, P1 and P2 each show a single band at the upper locus and the lower locus, and the positions are different. F1 shows both upper two bands and lower two bands, indicating that at each locus, double bands indicate heterozygosity and a single band indicates homozygosity. Observe F2 individual ①: both upper bands appear, so the upper locus is heterozygous; only one band appears in the lower part, and this band is the same as the lower band of F2 individual ④. Observe F2 individual ④: only the lower one of the upper bands appears, indicating homozygosity for the corresponding allele; the lower part also shows only the same band as ①, indicating homozygosity. Then reason: When ① is selfed, because the lower locus is already homozygous, all progeny maintain the same lower part as ④; the upper locus is heterozygous, and after selfing, the probability of producing the upper homozygous type required by ④ is 1/4. Therefore, the proportion of the selfed progeny of ① whose PCR electrophoresis result is the same as ④ is 1/4.
